claims.text: Premelting and melting temperatures in HEA nanoparticles are governed predominantly by local compositional fluctuations and short-range chemical ordering at surfaces and interfaces.
Local compositional fluctuations and short-range ordering alter local cohesive energies.
Local compositional fluctuations and short-range ordering initiate accelerated surface-atom mobility.
The proposed test material consists of uniform, single-phase, near-equiatomic nanoparticles containing three to five elements and minimal grain boundaries.
Controlling the initial elemental distribution during synthesis can vary local compositional heterogeneity and short-range ordering while retaining the same overall composition.
Short-range chemical heterogeneities can form, dissolve, or change under thermal treatment.
Concentrated alloys can contain local chemical clusters and non-random short-range order.
Short-range heterogeneities facilitate surface-driven atomic rearrangements and lower the barrier to melting at nanoparticle interfaces.
Localized compositional fluctuations reduce bonding stability near surfaces and interfaces.
Reduced near-surface bonding stability enhances atomic mobility and causes an earlier onset of premelting.
Melting subsequently progresses inward from the nanoparticle surface as temperature increases.
Nanoparticles with greater local compositional segregation will have a lower premelting onset temperature than compositionally homogeneous controls.
Nanoparticles with greater local compositional segregation will exhibit faster melt-front propagation than homogeneous controls.
The melting-onset difference between segregated and homogeneous nanoparticles could be on the order of tens of degrees Celsius.
The proposed effect should apply primarily to near-equiatomic systems containing at least five components with moderate enthalpic interactions.
Simpler alloys or systems with less entropic stabilization may be less sensitive to local chemical heterogeneity.
Particle-shape anisotropy, contaminants, and extensive grain-boundary networks are possible modifiers of the proposed mechanism.

Identical premelting onset and similar melting evolution in segregated and homogeneous particles of identical overall composition would falsify the proposed control by segregation and short-range ordering.
